high.title: Markets advance with US-Iran ceasefire; Ibovespa in dollar soars today (08)
high.summary: Brazilian markets surged strongly following a temporary two-week ceasefire agreement between the United States and Iran, which has significantly reduced geopolitical tensions and oil prices. The Ibovespa showed particularly strong performance when measured in dollar terms, benefiting from both the risk-on sentiment and potential BRL strength. Oil prices retreated below $100 per barrel as the truce paves the way for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route for global energy supplies. The ceasefire was brokered by Pakistan after Iran accepted a 10-point proposal, with President Trump announcing the suspension of planned military strikes. This development is highly bullish for Brazilian risk assets, as reduced geopolitical tensions typically drive capital flows toward emerging markets like Brazil. The relief in commodity markets, particularly oil, could also benefit Brazil's inflation outlook and provide the Central Bank with more policy flexibility. FX traders should monitor whether this risk-on sentiment sustains BRL strength against the USD.

high.title: Real Time: US-Iran truce moves market; Ibovespa tracks inflation and industry
high.summary: The Ibovespa is closely monitoring key inflation and economic activity indicators, including Brazil's IGP-DI inflation data and vehicle production figures, alongside global data from the Eurozone. Markets are particularly focused on the upcoming FOMC minutes from the US Federal Reserve, which could provide crucial insights into future monetary policy direction and impact BRL/USD dynamics. The US-Iran truce continues to support risk sentiment across Brazilian assets. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi confirmed that passage through the Strait of Hormuz would be reopened, further supporting the positive market mood and benefiting Brazilian equities and the real.
